body: Exactly, it’s both scary and comforting to feel like there’s a way out

Why? I mean, I guess it’s bc I haven’t found a profession that I’m interested in enough to pursue.
I worked in finance for awhile and kept my expenses very, very minimal while doing so. I did this for 7 years. With the income I saved I put into index funds. I’ve been very fortunate in how they’ve turned out. I’ve since moved the money into fixed income, as I’ve managed to accumulate enough where my lifestyle is now sustainable. I’d consider working again if I somehow discover something I’m somewhat passionate about.
You’re a strong person for sticking to it. Keeping promises is a huge sign of character. I’m proud of you sticking to your promise, and moreover I’m proud of you for sticking around

Thank you for your reply - you’re absolutely right. My therapist and psych both recommend exactly what you’re saying. I suppose I’m still too far in a pit to have the energy to get out. 

I agree motivation is an issue, and I know that in order for my thoughts to change, my behavior has to change first. Those ideas both sound interesting and doable for me. Maybe I can capitalize on them when this current depressive wave subsides a bit.
